calls.head: The Capitals want Wilson head to head with Suzuki
calls.body: At home, the Capitals keep sending Wilson’s line (Wilson, Tuch and Strome) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Spencer Carbery has been choosing strength on strength. Tonight the Canadiens’ first line is Suzuki, Caufield and Slafkovský.

surprises.head: Montréal couldn’t get good looks
surprises.body: Montréal usually gets some of the league’s most dangerous shots, and Washington usually gives up some of the league’s most dangerous shots. Not tonight: Montréal’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 5.0% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.7% (about 7.0% against Washington) and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 25 games.

story.head: The Capitals squeak past the Canadiens
paras: Ivan Miroshnichenko played his first game of the season, after missing the first six. Josh Anderson struck first for the Canadiens early in the first. Jordan Kyrou tied it 3:27 later. Lane Hutson put the Habs up 2-1, 3:19 later. Miroshnichenko tied it 2-2 on the power play late in the first. Alex Tuch put the Capitals up 3-2 shorthanded early in the second. Anderson scored again midway through the second to tie it 3-3. Justin Holl and Tuch scored 4:36 apart midway through the third to put the Capitals up 5-3. Nick Suzuki made it 5-4 on the power play with the goalie pulled with 1:39 left, but the Capitals held on. Tuch also had an assist.

The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way. Charlie Lindgren made 26 saves for the Capitals, and Jakub Dobeš allowed five goals on 23 shots. The Capitals improved to 4-3-0, and the Canadiens fell to 3-3-1.

items.text: Cole Hutson got the better of his brother Lane.
The Capitals bounced back after two straight losses.
